transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I just haven’t been able to shake this constant feeling since my friend was killed. It’s like guilt, fear, and anger are always there, and it hasn’t eased up the way people seemed to think it would.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities since your friend's death?

Yes. I avoid that intersection whenever I can. I’ll take a longer route just so I don’t have to go past it. And I’ve mostly stopped signing up for tours or safety meetings, because the conversations always seem to come back to what happened there, and I just can’t sit through that.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the moment your friend was killed?

Yes. Not like I’m actually back there, exactly, but something will set it off. A crosswalk signal, or hearing a truck growl past, even seeing one of those walking-tour maps… suddenly the whole scene is right there in my head. I can see my friend stepping off the curb before I can stop it.
Has your daily life or relationships been significantly impacted by these feelings and memories?

Yes, it has. I used to help organize programs at the senior center and keep track of some of the volunteer budgets, but I’ve had to step back from that because I just can’t keep up reliably anymore. And I’ve pulled away from the clubs and activities that used to fill my week. I’m just not as involved with people as I was.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yes. I used to really enjoy planning my garden beds, quilting with the ladies, going to the theater outings, even fussing and arguing at book club. Now I see those things on the calendar and I just… don’t feel much. It’s like they belong to a version of me I don’t quite know anymore.
Do you often find yourself being easily startled by small things, like a door slamming or a car horn?
I don’t know that I’d say often. I mean, I notice loud noises, but I haven’t really been keeping track of being startled like that. It’s not something I’m sure about.
Do you feel emotionally distant from others or like you're observing life without being fully a part of it?

Yes. Even when I’m sitting with people I’ve known for years at the senior center, I feel… apart from them. Like they’re all talking and laughing on one side of a window, and I’m on the other side watching it happen. I’m there, but I don’t feel fully in it.
Have you had difficulty maintaining your relationships with family or friends since your friend's death?

Yes. I still see people, but it’s harder to feel connected to them. Even with folks I’ve known for years at the senior center, I feel kind of separated, like they’re all talking together and I’m just sitting on the other side of a window watching. So I guess that has made relationships feel more distant.
Are there any activities that you used to find meaningful or enjoyable that you have completely stopped doing since your friend's death?

Yes. I used to do a lot of things that mattered to me—planning my garden beds, quilting with the ladies, going to theater outings, even book club. I used to enjoy arguing about the books, in a friendly way. Now I see those things on the calendar and I just feel almost nothing. It’s like they belong to someone I used to be.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of guilt, fear, and anger since your friend's death?
It’s been since she was killed on that walking tour… about two years and three months ago now. I’ve been carrying those feelings pretty much since then.
Are there any activities that you have not completely stopped but now find yourself doing less often since your friend's death?

Yes. I haven’t stopped everything completely, but I do them a lot less. I used to plan my garden beds and go quilt with the ladies, go to theater outings, book club—all of that. Now I’ll see it on the calendar and just feel kind of blank, like it’s not really mine anymore. So I skip things more often than I used to.
Do you often think that you're a bad person or that you're to blame for your friend's death?

Yes. I do. I keep going over it in my head, thinking if I’d chosen a different route, or if I’d pushed harder about that crossing, maybe she’d still be here. I know the driver did it, and I’m angry at him and at the town for letting that crossing be so unsafe, but I still end up blaming myself too.
Do you often think that you're worthless or that your life has no purpose since your friend's death?

I’m not sure I’d say worthless, exactly. I do feel lost sometimes, like the things that used to matter don’t pull me the same way. But I don’t usually think my whole life has no purpose. It’s more that I feel shaken and unsure of myself.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in the number of activities you participate in or the frequency of participation since your friend's death?

Yes, definitely. I still do some things, but much less than before. I used to be busy with my garden plans, quilting with the ladies, theater outings, book club… and now I see them on the calendar and I just feel almost nothing, like those belonged to the person I used to be.
Do you often think that you're incompetent or that you've failed in some important way since your friend's death?

Yes… I do feel like I failed her in an important way. I keep telling myself that if I’d picked a different route, or pushed harder about that crossing, maybe she’d still be alive. And then I get furious all over again at the driver, and at the town for letting that crossing be so unsafe.
Do you often think that you're a bad person or that you're to blame for things beyond your friend's death?

I don’t really think of myself as a bad person, no. And I don’t think I’m to blame for everything, if that’s what you mean. It’s more tied to what happened with her… I don’t usually carry that blame into other parts of my life.
Do you often think that you're permanently changed for the worse since your friend's death?
I’m not sure I’d say “permanently.” I do feel changed since it happened, but I don’t know that I can honestly say it’s forever. Some days it feels that way, but I can’t really tell.
Have you lost interest in activities that were once important to you?

Yes. I used to really care about things like planning my garden beds, quilting with the ladies, going to theater outings, book club… I’d look forward to them. Now I see them on the calendar and it’s like I feel almost nothing. Like those were things someone else did, not me.
